releases.notes: Payment plans: Settings → Payment plans keeps the office's saved plans (title, payments, every month or every 2 weeks, down payment Off/Optional/Required, patient portion range, only-when codes, offer on treatment plans) and the longest plan; treatment plans show the saved plans; New payment plan starts from one; every plan's dates follow the first payment's date. Accepted treatment plans open as accepted (chosen option marked, signature shown) with View signed PDF and Clear signature.

Texting beta 2: when a patient texts STOP, Open Dental's OK to text is set to No for the patients on that number, and START sets it back to Yes (a switch in Settings → Texting, on by default). Emoji in a text are written as [emoji] in Open Dental's comm log, which can't store them.

Texting beta 1: a shared Texts inbox for two-way texting through Telnyx, in test mode (staff phones only). Incoming texts land in Needs reply until someone replies or marks them done; read marks are per person; Hand off flags a thread and passes it to the front desk; internal notes; STOP and START honored; every text in or out goes to the Open Dental comm log. Needs edge 0.27.0 and the owner's Telnyx setup on the edge. Automatic texts, forms and plan links by text come in later betas.

Card payments release 4: statements and pay links. Send statement from the patient page (the family ledger by visit), a statement email with one Pay button, resends of unopened statements, the pay page behind the birthdate check (stored card or a new card, Pay a different amount, View statement), missed plan payments paid from the same page, and the Statements and Patients with balances tabs on the Payments page. Also carries release 3 (payment plans). Needs edge 0.26.0.

Card payments release 3: payment plans run by Diastema. The 2- and 3-payment cards set up from Present mode after signing (down payment today on the card, then the payments on their dates), New payment plan on the patient page, the daily charge at the office's charge hour with retries and past-due follow-ups, staff actions (Charge now, Skip, Move a date, Replace card, Pause, Cancel, Mark paid otherwise), the Payment plans tab, and an optional Open Dental payment plan mode. Needs edge 0.26.0.

Card payments: Diastema support can now see from its own dashboard whether Moolah's payment notices reach this office, and can turn on this office's secure address when card payments need it, so nobody at the office has to change a setting.

Card payments (beta, off until Diastema support sets up the office's Moolah account):
- Take a card payment on the office terminal from the patient page, posted to Open Dental with a receipt.
- Cards on file: save a patient's card on the new Cards card and charge it later, with the patient present or not.
- Pay now after a plan is signed: on the terminal, with a card on file or a new card on the presenting device, and on the online plan page.
- The Payments page: every card payment, whether it is in Open Dental, voids and refunds, and a No-shows list for appointments held with a card.
- Settings → Payments: payment types, receipts, card holds and the no-show fee, and Moolah's payment notices.
- Card payments are set up entirely by Diastema support: nothing to press at the office (Moolah's payment notices register by themselves).
- Card payments: Moolah's payment notices are checked against more signing forms, and Settings → Payments shows how the last one was signed.
- Card payments: Moolah's payment notices are registered again with a fresh key where an earlier beta kept the wrong one.
- Card payments: every payment notice from Moolah is now checked against Moolah's own records before anything is changed.

0.23.0 (stable): the owner's to-do list. Sign-in and Staff drawer PIN pad; readable name menu; office colors, logo and contact line on Settings > Practice; shared email sections editor with formatting; Send forms opens on the forms due, several consents in one send, Pick forms without consents; unscheduled treatment follow-ups only for treatment planned in the last 6 months; original due date on hover and click a due date to change it; Follow Up pop-up in the app's colors; shorter Treatment Plan rows, 10 per page; Take a photo on Signed on paper; Compliance spacing, Requirements delete/restore, Edit mode, citation line; attention dots instead of the drill bar; overlapping blocks and blockout notes on the visual schedule; the discount card says the saving; payment plans say payments, not months; collapsed terms in the Staff drawer; Back to Diastema as the staff member who unlocked the drawer; one toolbox for open and presented plans; staff can show hidden payment options (setting); the form editor preview loads again.

0.23.0-beta.1: the owner's to-do list. PIN pad on sign-in and the Staff drawer; readable name menu; staff can show hidden payment options (setting); unscheduled treatment follow-ups only for treatment planned in the last 6 months (setting); original due date on the changed-date flag and click a due date to change it; Follow Up pop-up in the app's colors; Send forms opens on the forms due, Pick forms without consents, several consents in one send; office colors, logo and contact line on Settings > Practice; shared email sections in the forms editor's style with formatting; shorter Treatment Plan rows, 10 per page; Take a photo on Signed on paper; Compliance spacing, Requirements delete/restore, Edit mode and the citation line; attention dots instead of the drill bar; overlapping blocks on the visual schedule and blockout notes; the form editor preview loads again.

0.22.0 to stable: the treatment presentation module (whole-mouth plans, presenting and signing, the owner's decisions and small items), plus everything since 0.17.0: patient forms (editor, consents and policies, procedure forms, the Library), Compliance, the QA fixes and the schedule, task and photo updates.

Treatment presentation (0.22.0-beta.5): present a saved treatment plan chairside, send it to the patient, file the signed plan, and follow through.

Present mode: a full-screen, patient-facing view of any saved Open Dental plan on a paired device, with payment-option overrides for this patient (managers by default), "Choose this", and a signature to accept. A plan must be signed to count as accepted, and a payment card is chosen before signing; a plan under every minimum shows one "Pay in full" card. The outcome (wants to think, declined, scheduled already) and its reason are recorded, with one comm log line per presentation.

Explanations and pictures: a plain-language "What is this?" per procedure group in English and Spanish (Settings → Patient forms → Procedure forms → Explanation), the patient's own X-rays and photos beside the plan (from Open Dental Images or the camera, 500 MB in all), and optional phases as a display grouping only.

Send by email: the plan goes to the patient on the office's patient address; they open it with the patient's own date of birth, choose a card and sign online. Staff see Sent, Viewed and Signed, "Changed in Open Dental since sent" with Resend, reminders on a schedule the office sets, and link expiry. Needs edge 0.22.1 on production before an office uses it.

Filing: a signed plan's PDF goes into the patient's Images under a chosen category, and the Open Dental plan can be marked signed. Both are settings, off by default: turn on File signed plans (and Mark the plan signed) in Settings → Treatment plans → Signed plans at the upgrade; plans signed before that are never filed. If Mark the plan signed is on, untick "Save signed Treatment Plans to PDF" in Open Dental's Setup so each plan has one PDF.

Follow through: unanswered plans start or bring forward the patient's follow-up after two days; a huddle badge on the Schedule shows today's patients with an unaccepted plan and the day's total; Analytics gains a plan funnel in plans and dollars, by presenter, option, case size and reason; Today gains a Treatment plans card; the Compliance Monday summary gains a plans section. Plans count for 12 months (Settings → Treatment plans → Follow through).

Also in this release: a visit with no procedures, or only exam, x-ray and cleaning codes (D0, D1), no longer counts as a treatment visit on Follow-ups and the Unscheduled Treatment list. Today's Presented reads "not yet booked". The Follow-ups page no longer shows the My Tasks card (tasks have their own tab). Staff-sent patient emails bypass the edge's per-address daily cap (edge 0.22.1).

Migrations 28 to 33. No new Open Dental writes except the two filing settings above and the comm log lines.

Compliance beta 3: trainings (HIPAA privacy and security, bloodborne pathogens, hazard communication, and reading the x-ray operating procedures; a new hire's first one is due 90 days after their hire date, then each year by Dec 31, and bloodborne pathogens and x-ray procedures never more than 12 months apart; upload a certificate or tap I've read this), required reading (a Library SOP page with required roles asks everyone in those roles to read it, and asks again when you publish a new version unless you choose Don't re-ask; managers see Read by N of M), the Monday summary email to everyone who manages compliance (what's overdue, due soon or failed, with names and dates only; set the day and hour in Settings), the inspection binder (one zip with a PDF of everything for the dates you choose, plus the cards and certificates as they were uploaded), and importing people and credentials from a spreadsheet. Migration 27. The summary email needs edge 0.21.0.

Compliance beta 2: the emergency kit (the office enters its contents; each drug and supply has its own expiry, amber 60 days out and red at 30; the monthly kit check; Replace keeps history and Used shows Restock needed), drills (medical every 6 months and fire every year, each fix becomes a task, everyone who took part gets it on their own record), and SOP owners on the Library's SOP pages (an owner, a review cycle and required roles; the review is a check for the owner). Checks never done get 30 days before they go overdue, and a manager can enter when a check was last done before Diastema tracked it. Migration 26. Needs edge 0.21.0, like beta 1.

Compliance beta 1: the Compliance page (people with roles, credentials with card photos and history, equipment with recurring checks, due checks as Tasks that complete only by logging, failed checks with a manager's task, the daily job, the Texas starter list of requirements), the Manage compliance permission and the compliance switch (needs Tasks; edge 0.21.0 must know it). Migration 25.

Diastema's consents, before-visit and aftercare pages are ready to use from the start (published as the office's own, editable). New Fillings consent in English and Spanish. Aftercare pain advice filled in. Settings → Patient forms lists Consents and Pages under their own headings. Procedure forms groups pick code groups. Patient page Send forms → Consent: any consent with a tooth, quadrant or arch picker and the dentist.

Ready-made consents and pages can be used as they are (Use as is). Procedure forms settings in two panes, with code groups to pick from. Tasks: steps to check off and the newest comments in the list. Visual schedule shows blockouts with their titles. Patient page: Photo, one picture or a multi-page PDF into the patient's Images.

Fixes from the October 18 QA pass. Patient form answers are checked before they reach Open Dental (dates can't be in the future, hidden characters and emoji are removed, states must be real) and Undo works even when Open Dental changed the note. Settings refuse bad GapCheck codes and numbers instead of breaking the GapCheck screen, and two tabs saving the same settings no longer overwrite each other silently. Every date in an address or a form is checked the same way. A tab locks as soon as another tab signs out. Security headers on the staff app. Follow-up dates can't be set in the past, and a moved follow-up says who moved it, when, and what the schedule had. Patient search finds a first name on its own. Reopening a done weekly task no longer makes a duplicate. Cancelled form packets say so instead of 'complete'. Keyboard and screen-reader fixes across dialogs and menus.

0.20.0-beta.3: Stage 5 beta 3, the last of Stage 5. The Library (a new menu item): Patient forms, Procedure forms, Setup sheets, SOPs and Files, search in both languages, print any document blank or several together as a packet, an English/Spanish switch, uploads of PDFs and photos (migration 20). Setup sheets: a Setup sheet column and single-code links in Settings → Procedure forms, the Setup tag on the schedule, every sheet for an appointment under a header with the patient's alerts from Open Dental, Today's setups by operatory. Permissions Edit library (managers) and Edit setup sheets. Diastema's generic starters: 13 consents, 7 before-visit pages and 15 aftercare pages in English and Spanish, drafts to take or ignore; nothing is sent until the office publishes its own. SOP owners, review dates and required reading come with Compliance.

0.20.0-beta.2: Stage 5 beta 2. The dentist's co-sign on the staff side (Settings → People: Signs consents as; filing waits for the co-sign, or files with a note after the visit day). Print any published document, blank or filled in for a patient and appointment. Signed on paper files the photo and counts as signed. Changed after signing turns the badge red and adds a fresh consent (no automatic email). Planned treatment consents ready to sign. Sending: three timeline steps (Procedure forms 3 days before, a reminder the day before while unsigned, Aftercare when the appointment is set complete), two letters with Edit template, comm log lines for sends and reads, the aftercare page on the one link with Save as PDF. The Forms card's Changes from forms fits a phone screen. Migration 19. Real sends need edge 0.20.0.

0.20.0-beta.1: Stage 5 beta 1, procedure forms with badges only. Settings → Patient forms → Procedure forms: one table tying code groups to consents, before-visit and aftercare pages (16 starter rows, documents to pick). Appointments' procedures are read and matched; the schedule badge turns grey, amber or red for consents needed; a This visit block on the patient page; Follow-ups → Consents needed today (switch in the table's page); Sign now hands the device to the patient for this visit's consents and before-visit page; coverage rules (until done, for N months, until a new version). A procedure consent may publish with its Spanish still a draft. Import a file now takes a bundle of documents; Summerbrook's Flex consents and post-op pages come in that way. No sending yet (beta 2). Migration 18 part 1.

0.19.0-beta.4: intake editor round 2. Canvas: Undo and Redo, Delete on added items, grey-out or hide the other packet's items, the Update explained, no scroll jump on redraws. Tabs: add and remove a condition category, one Referrals tick list. Text editor: centre or right alignment, the language picker. Policies: Refuse ends without a signature (the PDF says who refused and when), checkboxes and initials boxes in a policy's summary (the exam consent and office policy starters move theirs there). Publish is disabled with no changes; Discard fixed, also from History.

0.19.0-beta.3: the intake editor revamp. The form canvas: the whole form in one list with Parts and Steps, a live phone preview beside it, a question's card opening in place, ready-made pieces, drag to reorder, where each answer goes in Open Dental, View as New patient or Update, a language picker and Translations tab, and the Conditions, Medications, Allergies and Referrals lists on tabs. Consents and pages are written as text, with risks initialled one by one, steps, Call us if lines, pictures and required confirmations; an older block consent or page offers a one-click conversion; the block editor is gone. The health form (version 3) asks one Yes or No before the nine condition groups: No skips them all and counts as No for each; on an Update it clears only the problems that were offered.

Consents are now documents. Settings → Patient forms → Forms has a Policies group: the privacy notice, the consent for exam and X-rays and the office policy, each its own document, read and signed one after the other. Edit opens a simple text editor: paste your text from Word or Google Docs (fonts, colours, tables and pictures are left out), format it with headings, bold, italic, underline, lists, sizes and links, and use Insert for a checkbox, an initials box, or your practice's name, address, phone or email. English and Spanish are side by side, with a phone preview. New policy adds one; drag to change the order. Patients read each policy as one page (a short summary first when you set one), and after the first signature each next policy signs with one tap. Each signed policy is its own PDF in Open Dental with its whole text. Who we may discuss care with and detailed voicemails are now on the New patient form. Your current consents are converted on update, word for word.

The form editor. Settings → Patient forms → Forms lists every form, consent and page; Edit opens one full width to reword, reorder, switch off or add questions in English and Spanish, fill in your consents' blanks, see it on a phone as you type, and publish a new version. Patients part way through finish the version they started; for a consent you choose whether signed patients sign again. History, Compare and Restore keep every version; Export and Import move a form to another office. Consents and pages can hold risk lists with initials, steps, a Call us if box and pictures, ready for procedure consents. Patient emails are in the same editor: Edit template on each email step of Settings → Patient email changes that email's words and subject, with a preview in both languages and Send me a test; the greeting, appointment lines, forms section and Confirm section are shared by every email and changed once. The problems, starter lists and urgent medical note list moved into the editor, beside the health questions.

Patient forms, ready for the form editor. The New patient form and the health history update are now one form, asked as either. Every office starts from Diastema's generic consents and email subjects: the consents have blanks for your practice's details and policy numbers, and they can't be sent to patients until your own wording is filled in. Diastema keeps a signed form's answers, signature and PDF for 30 days after it's filed in Open Dental, then only that it was signed and when. Patient emails record which wording they went out with.

Settings → Practice (one place for the practice's name, address, email and phone); the privacy notice's facts as text in the notice; Patient email timeline as step tabs with each recall its own step; Diastema emailed / texted / confirmed statuses in Open Dental; Send forms in one click (Email, Text, Open on this device, Copy link); a Save question before leaving changed settings; Open Dental's button with no patient picked opens the home page.

Patient forms online and patient email: welcome letters with the forms link, appointment reminders and email confirmations, with Preview only to check them first. Both stay off until Diastema support turns them on. Settings → Office → Updates now saves a change of channel or overnight installs.
The installer checks that its port is free and offers another if a program already uses it. Setup finds Open Dental's API service on this computer and says whether the address works.

Setup checks the Open Dental API address for you: it looks for Open Dental's API service on this computer and says whether the address works. The installer checks that its port is free and offers another if a program already uses it.

GapCheck labels now say what's on file in Open Dental, not what insurance covers: "over limit" instead of "not covered", "At limit" instead of "Not due", and totals "within plan limits". Monthly usage figures are sent for each finished month. Missed calls go straight to your office's own secure address. If Diastema is ever stopped or suspended, an administrator can still open and export your records.

GapCheck: the X-ray check is now called GapCheck. New servers set up with one enrollment code from Diastema; new staff get temporary PINs; a printable post-install packet. When Open Dental refuses its keys, the setup page says where to add them.

Diastema now shows the features your office has. Diastema support turns them on or off; a feature that's off is hidden and its data is kept, and one on for a trial has a Preview tag.

Settings is now a few short pages: one for each feature with settings, plus People (who signs in and what each level can do) and Office (Open Dental, devices and the secure address, backups, updates, the Diastema connection and support). Settings that rarely change are under More settings.

Missed calls: the old WordPress mailbox is gone. If your office still used it, Settings → Missed calls offers Diastema's mailbox.

The support file no longer includes the office's certificate keys.

Usage statistics: when your server is connected to Diastema, it now sends Diastema a short daily summary of how much each part of Diastema was used (for example pages opened, treatment plans printed, follow-ups logged and X-ray fixes), day totals in dollars for the X-ray check and printed plans, how many staff signed in, and a few settings. It never includes patient names or details, staff names, or anything typed into Diastema. This helps Diastema decide what to improve.

Updates from Diastema support: when your server is connected to Diastema, Diastema support can now install an update for you (usually overnight, at the install time in Settings → About), go back to an earlier version if an update causes trouble, and adjust your update settings. Settings → About shows anything scheduled and who installed the last update. As always, only updates signed by Diastema are installed, your data is backed up first, and the previous version is put back automatically if a new one doesn't start.

One address for everyone: the office's computers can now use your office's secure address too, like iPads and phones. Add each computer once (Settings → Devices; admins can make one code for several computers). Browsers use HTTP/2 through it, so each page loads over a single connection. The office-network address (http://SERVER:8080) becomes an advanced option in Settings → About: it always works on the server itself, and for other computers only while an admin has it on, for example while the internet is down. It stays on after this update until you turn it off, so nothing changes until you're ready. The Open Dental button can now open the secure address (Settings → About shows the path to use).

iPads, phones and computers are added once, then open Diastema at your office's secure address from anywhere, not just on the office's internet connection. Add one from Settings → Devices (scan the QR code with the device, or type the short code on it), or, on the office's internet connection, tap "Ask to add it" on the device and approve it from the banner after checking the number on its screen. Managers and admins can add and remove devices (Settings → Users & access). After this update, each iPad and phone that already uses the secure address needs to be added once. Everyone still signs in with their PIN; 10 wrong PINs in a row on one device remove it. Computers using the office-network address aren't affected.

iPads and phones connect more reliably. Diastema's connection to diastema.app now uses secure WebSockets, the standard that office firewalls and web filters already allow, and an iPad's or phone's first request no longer fails after the office has been quiet for a few minutes. Update the server soon: diastema.app now expects this kind of connection, so iPads and phones can't reach Diastema through it until the server is updated. Computers in the office aren't affected.

iPads and phones in the office: an admin can turn it on in Settings → About. Staff then open Diastema on an iPad or phone on the office Wi-Fi at your office's own address (shown there, with a QR code to scan), with a real certificate that this server holds and renews on its own. Everyone still signs in with their PIN. Computers in the office keep using Diastema exactly as before, even when the internet is down.

Off-site copies with Diastema: an admin can tick “Also keep an off-site copy with Diastema” on the Automatic backups card (Settings → Backup & restore; needs the Diastema connection). Each night's backup file, still locked with the recovery code, also goes to Diastema's off-site storage and is kept 14 days. A fresh install can restore from it on the setup page with a restore code from Diastema support.

Missed calls can now go through Diastema's own mailbox instead of the WordPress plugin: Settings → Phone calls → Switch to Diastema's mailbox, then paste the new webhook address into Mango. The WordPress mailbox is still emptied until you stop it, so no call is lost while you change Mango.

Connected to Diastema: an admin can connect this server in Settings → About with a one-time enrollment code from Diastema. Once connected it sends a short status every 15 minutes (versions, whether Open Dental answers, backups on or off), never patient data.
First-run setup now ends with an optional step to add the Diastema button to Open Dental (Skip for now to do it later in Settings → About). The Open Dental button steps also fit on phone screens.

Open Dental button: Settings → About → Open Dental button walks admins through adding a Diastema button to Open Dental's toolbar (values ready to copy, a button icon to download, and a check that it's set up). Clicking it opens the selected patient's Diastema page.

New: Settings > About > Go back to an earlier version (admins). Pick any earlier release that works with your data (0.5.0-beta.11 or newer; beta channel lists betas and stable, stable lists stable) with its release notes. Diastema backs up the database, installs it, and puts the current version back if the earlier one doesn't start. Overnight automatic updates are turned off so the version you left doesn't come right back.

New: Settings > Backup & restore (admins). Download backup makes one password-protected file with everything needed to bring Diastema back after a failed update, a reinstall or a move to a new server (users and PINs, follow-ups, tasks, history, settings, header image, the Open Dental connection and the phone-calls pairing). Restore from Settings, or from the setup page of a fresh install ('Restore from a backup file instead'): the file and password are checked first, Diastema restarts to finish, and the data it replaced is kept in backups\before-restore-...

Analytics: 'No comparison' option (no earlier periods loaded, no comparison table, faster). When comparing with 2 or more earlier periods, each tile shows a mini column chart of those periods and this one (hover a bar for its value). The comparison table is now folded under 'Show the numbers' (remembered).

Analytics: new 'Compare with' setting (previous 1 to 5 periods, remembered per device) and a comparison table with each key stat for this period, each earlier period, their average and the change. With more than one period the tiles compare against the average. Earlier periods now line up with the calendar (months with months, quarters with quarters, month-to-date with the same days of earlier months, a single day with the same weekday in earlier weeks).

Schedule: new Visual view (List / Visual switch, remembered per device). One column per shown operatory, always fitting the screen width, with each appointment as tall as its length, colored by kind of visit (checkup/cleaning, treatment, new patient, limited/emergency, or the color set in Open Dental). Blocks without room for details shrink to initials; tap one for its details and an Open patient button. Double-booked appointments sit side by side, today shows a red line at the current time, and - / + make the day taller or shorter.

Schedule on phones: each appointment is now a compact card (time, patient, age and badges, operatory and providers, procedures on one line, note) instead of one labelled line per field, so busy days need far less scrolling. Long appointment notes start cut to 2 lines on phones and 3 on desktop, with More / Less to see the whole note.
Fix: on the Schedule, the Today button's text no longer spills outside the button, and the date box no longer makes the page scroll sideways on phones.

New layout. Home is now the day Schedule: appointments with time, operatory, dentist/hygienist, procedures, confirmation and notes; previous/next day, Today and a date picker; show/hide operatories and hide completed (remembered on each device). Clicking a patient opens the new Patient page: follow-up status (with the full follow-up window), saved treatment plans (print as before), unscheduled treatment, appointments and tasks. Patient search is in the top bar on every page (press / to jump to it). 'Today' is renamed Follow-ups; the separate Treatment Plans page is gone.
X-ray audit: only exams with missed or removed X-rays are listed (the summary still counts every exam in the date range). The 'All exams' view is gone; the CSV download has the same problem exams.

Follow-ups: patients with anything other than a checkup or cleaning on the schedule (any code outside D0/D1, including office N-codes, or an appointment with no procedures) no longer come up as due on Today. Once that appointment has passed, if the treatment still isn't scheduled or done, the follow-up comes due again.

X-ray check: a comprehensive exam (D0150) visit with 4BW and 3 or more PAs now counts as an FMX, so it uses up the pano/FMX frequency (insurance may treat it as a full mouth series). Shown as the last pano/FMX where it applies. Settings > X-ray check can turn it off or change the exam codes and number of PAs.

Diastema 0.5.0. New since 0.4.0: X-ray check (bitewings, pano/FMX and extra PAs due at upcoming periodic exams by insurance frequency; one-click fix to add or remove X-rays on the appointment with undo and a running total; audit of past exams). Setup codes for connecting to Open Dental (or your own developer key), with keys encrypted on the server. Phone calls: missed calls from Mango Voice become tasks. Download support file. Fixes to the task window and updater.

New: Settings > About > Download support file (admins): version, settings, an Open Dental connection check, service logs and update history, with no keys, secrets, database contents or patient information (phone numbers and emails in logs are masked). Uninstaller now also removes the update task and downloaded updates, makes sure Diastema has stopped, and supports /DELETEDATA for silent uninstalls.
Fix: in the task window, the patient search list was cut off by the bottom of the window.

Phone calls: made for Mango Voice. Settings > Phone calls shows the full Mango webhook URL (with Mango's {CALLER_NUMBER}, {TIME_UTC} etc.). Each missed call becomes a task 'Missed phone call from (xxx) xxx-xxxx at 2:14 PM' for the person you choose, with caller ID and the line called in the notes. No patient matching. A repeated webhook for the same call is ignored.

New: Settings > Phone calls. Missed calls from the phone system (e.g. Mango Voice) become tasks: the phone system posts to the Diastema Connect mailbox on your website, where each call is encrypted for this office; Diastema collects every 30 seconds, matches the number to patients (caller first), and merges repeat calls into the open task. Off until paired and turned on.

Open Dental connection: offices can now connect with a single setup code from their Diastema provider, or (advanced) their own developer key. Saved keys are encrypted for the server (existing installs are encrypted 10 minutes after starting). About shows which kind of key is in use. If the data folder moves to another server, setup asks for the code again and keeps everything else.

X-ray audit: each past exam now shows the same reasoning as upcoming exams - the insurance frequency and how much was used, the last X-ray, when it was next allowed, and how many PAs would have fit (flagging when more were taken than fit).
X-ray audit: removed X-rays are listed only when insurance would have paid and no X-ray of that kind was done instead.
X-ray audit: removed X-rays that insurance wouldn't have paid for are no longer listed or counted.

X-ray check: new 'Audit past exams' tab (read-only). For completed periodic exams in a date range it shows what insurance would have paid for that wasn't done (bitewings, pano/FMX, PAs that would have fit), and X-rays removed from the appointment with who deleted them and when (flagging the day of the visit). CSV download. New permission 'Run the X-ray audit' (on for Managers).

X-ray check: running total of what the fix button has added (at each patient's fee schedule), how much of it is completed, and planned X-rays removed that insurance wouldn't pay. Managers and Admins can clear it to start over; the change history is kept.

X-ray check: the fix now adds the PAs that fit with bitewings (D0220 for the first, D0230 for each additional) on default teeth set in Settings (#8 and #24). Each appointment shows what the fix is worth at the patient's fee schedule, and the page shows the total in covered X-rays not yet scheduled.

X-ray check: one button per appointment adds the bitewings / pano that are due, or removes planned X-rays insurance won't cover and extra PAs. Undo for the last click. New access permission: Add or remove X-rays on appointments (on for Staff and Managers).

X-ray check: when bitewings are due or scheduled, shows how many extra PAs (up to 2) can be taken while bitewings + PAs stay under the FMX / pano fee at the patient's insurance fee schedule, and flags appointments with more PAs scheduled than fit. The comparison (lower of FMX and pano, FMX only, or pano only) is in Settings → X-ray check.

X-ray check now covers panos too: pano and FMX share one frequency, so the last pano or FMX decides when a new pano is allowed. Also flags X-rays allowed within 30 days after an exam (moving the appointment could get them covered) and plan frequencies that look mistyped in Open Dental.

New: X-ray check tab. Lists periodic exams in the next 4 weeks and whether bitewings are due under each patient's insurance BW frequency (from the last 4BW or FMX, including other-office X-rays in Insurance History). Flags bitewings already on an appointment that insurance won't cover yet.
Fixes: an update now finishes cleanly (the About page shows the result right away instead of 'Installing…'), and the page reloads only once after an update.
Test update: confirms updates install through Settings → About. No other changes.

First release with automatic updates. Settings → About now shows available updates, lets admins install them, and can install them overnight. Also includes the fix for the data-folder permissions during installation.
